title: Diagnosing Localized Low Water Pressure: Clogged Aerator Screen
description: Before assuming your main supply line has lost pressure, check whether the issue affects one fixture or the entire building. When low flow is limited to a single sink, the cause is usually a clogged aerator rather than a main pressure failure. Mineral scale and fine sediment accumulate inside the aerator mesh screen, drastically reducing the cross-sectional area available for water flow. Removing the aerator, cleaning the sediment, and soaking the mesh stack in vinegar to dissolve calcium deposits typically restores normal volume immediately. Always check aerator screens first during initial diagnostic calls. What fixture in your home currently has low flow?
image_prompt: High-detail educational macro photograph showing a cutaway view of a modern brass faucet spout tip in a professional plumbing workshop setting. Vertical 9:16 composition. The metal spout wall is visually sliced to reveal the interior aerator assembly, including the rubber sealing washer, perforated plastic flow restrictor disc, and fine stainless steel mesh screens. White calcium mineral scale buildup and dark sand sediment are visible lodged on top of the upper mesh layer, blocking the water passages. Micro-droplets of water trail beneath the screen. Realistic metallic textures, sharp macro focus, neutral workshop lighting, clean composition centered in frame with ample clean background space at the top and bottom thirds. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no diagrams.
visual_story: The visual focuses on a cross-sectional view of a faucet nozzle to demonstrate how debris restricts dynamic flow. The viewer notices how fine mineral scale and grit collect right above the aerator screen stack inside the spout. This visually proves that high pressure can exist behind the restriction, but physical blockage limits water flow rate at the outlet. This helps learners distinguish between systemic water pressure loss and localized physical flow restrictions.

on_image_text.hook: Low Water Pressure at Just One Faucet?
on_image_text.explanation: Trapped sediment and scale inside the aerator mesh restrict water flow without affecting main supply pressure.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect and clean aerator screens before altering pressure valves or main lines.
